absent: Physical command encoding, queue mechanics, and error recovery for ITS commands.
Layout and lifetime of ITS nodes, devices, collections, virtual machines, and virtual processors.
Redistributor and property table discovery, sizing, and initial mapping.
MSI descriptor structure and address programming mechanics.
Doorbell identifier values and move command wire format.
Timeout or recovery behavior when synchronization polling never completes.
Callers and locking context for mask, unmask, affinity, and virtual affinity entry points.

findings.text: A controller interface named ITS bundles masking, unmasking, affinity control, message composition, pending state handling, retrigger, and virtual CPU dispatch for the generic interrupt layer, delegating completion signaling to its parent.

Interrupt enablement and priority live in a byte array indexed by identifier minus the architectural base; forwarded interrupts use a per virtual machine page plus a cached copy while others use the shared redistributor table; each update clears selected bits, sets selected bits, always asserts the group flag, then enforces visibility with either a cache clean or a barrier based on platform needs.
Property changes are followed by an invalidation chosen from direct redistributor access, physical command, or virtual command depending on direct support, hardware generation, and forwarding state.

Direct invalidation pins the routing processor, locks its redistributor, writes either a physical identifier or a virtual tuple combining validity plus virtual processor identity plus virtual identifier, then polls a sync flag with relaxed waits until the redistributor acknowledges.

Device events rest in physical or virtual states; map from physical allocates virtual state, pins the virtual machine, marks forwarding, publishes properties, replaces physical with virtual mapping, and counts the virtual interrupt, while map from virtual only moves; property updates rewrite config with optional invalidate and doorbell sync; unmap restores physical state and releases resources when the last virtual interrupt departs; get copies stored mapping without transition.

Virtual machine attachment per translation list is reference counted; eager configurations keep all virtual processors mapped permanently while lazy ones map every processor with a full invalidate on first use and unmap all on final release.

Coordinated virtual processor moves serialize on a dedicated lock, stamp each descriptor with an increasing sequence value, and fan out in list order to every capable node with its own destination collection, while simple topologies address only the leading node.

Virtual cache maintenance for a whole processor and per doorbell invalidation take processor scope, while per event virtual invalidate, trigger, and clear reuse physical event semantics but pair them with virtual synchronization rather than physical.

Free identifiers form a sorted linked list of segments each storing a base and a length; allocation consumes from the first fitting segment and discards emptied ones, release inserts in order and fuses with neighbors when contiguous.

Identifier width caps at 16 bits for 64K values, usable allocation begins at 8192 past the reserved low range, and the distributor capability register encodes its restricted count as a small shifted field plus one.
Per processor load splits into managed and unmanaged atomic counters selected by affinity state, and target choice scans candidates for the lowest count with earliest wins on ties.

Unmanaged targets prefer node overlap with requested and online sets before widening to requested online overlap and finally any online processor, managed targets start from requested affinity with optional node narrowing, a platform workaround can forbid cross socket search, forwarded interrupts reject affinity changes, moves issue only on processor change, and effective affinity recording is configuration dependent.

The message signaled interrupt translator address derives from the node physical base plus a fixed translator offset through a per node accessor, and message composition stores the event identifier as payload while delegating address programming to the MSI descriptor.

Only pending state is supported; asserting uses trigger commands and clearing uses clear commands, selecting virtual or physical variants by forwarding state, and retrigger asserts pending while converting the status result into a boolean outcome.

A static spinlock with interrupt save guards the shared affinity scratch mask, direct redistributor updates pair processor pinning with the target lock, virtual affinity dispatch holds the device virtual lock, virtual machine attach combines the machine lock with per processor locks, and identifier range edits serialize on a mutex.

The shared scratch mask corrupts under concurrent use without its lock, unordered virtual processor moves break list consistency, property bytes stay stale without explicit visibility maintenance, and sync polling never times out so an unresponsive redistributor stalls the caller indefinitely.

Masking first disables the doorbell then clears enablement while unmasking reverses the order; doorbell handling is inert on newer hardware, skips redundant requests, records state, and retunes mapping through a same processor move to avoid recreating an existing association.

Virtual processor affinity requires capable hardware, routes map, query, and property commands to dedicated handlers under the device virtual lock, interprets missing command info as unmap, and rejects unknown command kinds.
Startup capacity derives from identifier width minus the reserved base, clamps to a hypervisor reported bound when sane, and seeds the free list with one range spanning all usable identifiers.
